def: Of a result, able to be regenerated from its record, exactly or within a stated tolerance.
A directory with its own Python interpreter link and installed packages, keeping one project's dependencies separate from others.
A file recording the exact version of every installed package, including indirect dependencies, so an environment can be rebuilt identically.
A deterministic procedure that turns a seed into a long sequence of numbers that behave like random ones.
The starting value of a pseudorandom number generator; the same seed gives the same sequence.
Variables held in a running notebook kernel that influence results but are not visible in the cells as written.
A record of each run's code version, data identifier, configuration, environment, seed and results.
A short fingerprint computed from a file's bytes that changes whenever the contents change.
Producing identical output bytes on a rerun, which is hard to guarantee for parallel or GPU code.
Producing a rerun result that falls within the normal run-to-run variation, even if it is not identical.
